skill.name: codex-pet
skill.description: Create a Codex-compatible custom pet from one reference image using RunComfy and ImageMagick. The skill documents generating a canonical pose, building a 9-row sprite atlas, creating pet.json, and installing the files into the Codex pets directory.
skill.summary: Build Codex Pet sprite sheets and manifests with RunComfy.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown backtick false positives, but the skill legitimately documents local CLI execution, credential handling, remote image processing, and writes into Codex hidden pet directories. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md. The highest contextual issue is that PET_NAME is used in shell paths without validation, which can permit writes outside the intended pet folder.

remediation.issue: PET_NAME is used directly in local paths.
remediation.suggestion: Validate pet names with a strict allowlist such as lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens before using them in RUN_DIR or DEST.

remediation.issue: The workflow requires external CLI commands and package installation.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running npx, npm, brew, apt-get, runcomfy, magick, mkdir, cat, or cp commands.

remediation.issue: Source images are processed by a third-party service.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to provide private images or private URLs, and document the RunComfy and OpenAI processing boundary clearly.

remediation.issue: RunComfy credentials may be stored in hidden config files or environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Document token rotation, avoid logging token-bearing commands, and prefer least-privilege tokens where supported.

content.user_title: Create Custom Codex Pets with RunComfy
content.value_statement: Custom Codex Pets need exact sprite sheets and manifests. This skill turns one reference image into Codex-ready pet files using RunComfy and ImageMagick.
actual_capabilities: Generates a canonical Codex Pet pose through the RunComfy GPT Image 2 edit endpoint.
Builds a 1536x1872 sprite atlas with 9 Codex animation rows.
Creates a pet.json manifest that points Codex to spritesheet.webp.
Documents installation into the local Codex pets directory.
Explains chroma-key cleanup and small ImageMagick animation transforms.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy token or login, ImageMagick, and a public source image URL.
Sends the source image URL to RunComfy for remote image processing.
Uses one generated pose with transforms, so motion is subtle instead of frame-specific.
The shell examples need pet name validation before automated use.

use_cases.title: Build a Personal Codex Pet
use_cases.description: Turn a personal mascot or avatar into files that Codex can load as a desktop pet.

use_cases.title: Prepare Branded Team Pets
use_cases.description: Create consistent Codex Pet assets for internal developer tools or team demos.

use_cases.title: Prototype Sprite Atlases
use_cases.description: Generate a first-pass Codex Pet atlas, then tune animation rows and chroma-key settings.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Pet
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup with one reference image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Codex Pet skill to create a custom pet from this public image URL. Name it demo-pet.

prompt_templates.title: Match a Mascot Style
prompt_templates.scenario: Control the visual identity of the generated pet.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Codex Pet from this mascot image. Preserve the main colors, glasses, and simple friendly expression.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Animation Rows
prompt_templates.scenario: Adjust motion after the first atlas is generated.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the generated Codex Pet atlas and suggest small ImageMagick transform changes for a stronger idle bob.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Pet Planning
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for several source images.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a safe batch workflow for five Codex Pets. Include pet name validation, output folders, and token handling.

output_examples.input: A public URL for a mascot image and the pet name build-helper.
output_examples.output: A generated Codex Pet folder containing a WebP sprite sheet and manifest ready for local Codex installation.

output_examples.input: A generated pet with weak movement in the idle row.
output_examples.output: A concise set of transform changes, such as a slightly larger vertical shift and a slower blink cadence.

output_examples.input: A private team wants multiple branded Codex Pets.
output_examples.output: A workflow checklist covering source images, validated pet names, RunComfy token handling, and final file review.

best_practices: Use only public, non-sensitive source images because remote services process the image URL.
Validate pet names with a strict allowlist before running shell examples.
Review generated sprite sheets before copying them into the Codex pets directory.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets into prompts, file names, or command history.
Do not use pet names that contain slashes, dots, spaces, or shell metacharacters.
Do not run global install commands in automated environments without approval.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a Codex Pet sprite sheet and manifest that Codex can load as a custom desktop pet.

faq.question: Does it require Codex Pro image generation?
faq.answer: No. It uses RunComfy with GPT Image 2 and ImageMagick instead of the Codex imagegen skill.

faq.question: What tools must be installed?
faq.answer: The workflow expects the RunComfy CLI, ImageMagick, and a RunComfy login or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN.

faq.question: Where are the generated files installed?
faq.answer: The documented workflow copies pet.json and spritesheet.webp into the local Codex pets directory.

faq.question: Can it create dramatic frame-by-frame animation?
faq.answer: No. It uses one generated pose and small transforms, so the animation is intentionally subtle.

faq.question: Is it safe to use private images?
faq.answer: Use caution. The source image URL is processed by RunComfy, so private or sensitive images are not recommended.
